name: Lapis-Permafrost
description: Lapis-Permafrost is a small, intensely blue ice world, its surface stained by cyanide compounds frozen into the upper ice layers, creating a coloration reminiscent of lapis lazuli stone. The low gravity allows ice formations to grow into improbable spires and arches, some reaching hundreds of meters before their own weight overcomes the crystal structure. Methane lakes pool in sheltered craters, their surfaces frozen into dark mirrors.

The thin atmosphere is insufficient to carry sound more than a few meters, and the surface exists in near-silence broken only by the occasional crack of shifting ice. Solar wind has carved the exposed ice faces into aerodynamic forms, smooth curves and tapering points that all orient toward the distant star. The blue coloration is deepest in shadow, where the cyanide ice takes on the saturated indigo of twilight.

Lapis-Permafrost's remoteness and minimal resource value have made it an ideal location for a smuggling cache, hidden within the crystal cavern networks where the natural labyrinth of ice tunnels defeats casual searchers. The cache is rumored to belong to a syndicate specializing in restricted xenoarchaeological artifacts, using the frozen world as a waystation between dig sites and black-market buyers.

The planet's only regular visitors are the smugglers and the occasional ice-research survey. Law enforcement has little reason to patrol this far from established routes, and the natural defenses of extreme cold, labyrinthine caverns, and minimal atmosphere make interdiction impractical. Lapis-Permafrost will likely remain a blue whisper at the edge of known space, noticed by few, remembered by fewer.
